Subject: Post-call: deployment mode & compliance checklist for PulseWell

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we keep momentum: 

Call highlights:
- Primary constraint: PHI flow for scheduled claims processing and patient summaries (BAA required).
- Latency target: 150ms p95 for inference on typical 512-token prompts; batch processing for high-throughput back-office jobs is expected.
- Preferred initial rollout: Hosted API for non-PHI workloads, Dedicated capacity or Private VPC for PHI with BAA — team wants options and cost tradeoffs.

Immediate asks (owner / due):
1) We will share a short compliance pack (SOC2 summary + BAA draft) — Priya (today).
2) Security questionnaire: PulseWell to confirm whether SSO + IP allowlisting are mandatory for production — Elena (by 12/3).
3) Architecture decision: if on-prem required, schedule a technical deep-dive with Rishi and your infra lead — Priya/Rishi (propose slots 12/6–12/8).

Attachments I'm sending with this thread: BAA_draft_PulseWell_20261129.pdf, SOC2_summary_Redwood_20261129.pdf, deployment-options-matrix.xlsx

Next immediate step: I'll follow up with the BAA + SOC2 summary (attached) and a one-page decision matrix that shows cost/latency tradeoffs across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Would love confirmation on who from PulseWell will handle procurement (cc'd) and who will own security review.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Priya — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirming PHI: yes, claims payloads that include patient identifiers will be PHI and must be covered by a signed BAA.
- SSO is mandatory for production; IP allowlisting preferred but we can accept private peering/VPC as an alternative.
- Procurement: that's me looped with procurement@pulsewell.health (they want a ballpark for monthly committed spend for Dedicated).

Quick asks: can you include an explicit list of SOC2 artifacts we can hand to our auditors (system ops, access logs, incident response runbooks, and data retention policies)? Also curious if Redwood supports KMS-backed key management in Private deployments.

I can join the technical deep-dive if scheduled before 12/8.

—Elena

Quick internal note and proposed artifact mapping (sending to Elena for visibility):

Mapped artifacts we typically provide to auditors: 
- Access control: IAM policies, SSO config screenshots, periodic access review logs.
- Logging & monitoring: token-level request logs (retention window), aggregated lat/err metrics, trace samples (PII redacted).
- Incident response: IR playbook, example postmortem (redacted), contact matrix.
- Change management: deploy approvals, release notes for runtime changes.
- Environment separation: network diagrams showing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, and data flow for PHI exclusion/inclusion.

Notes: Private VPC/on-prem deployments can include KMS-backed keys and an on-prem audit collector for your auditors. For Hosted+Dedicated we supply a SOC2 report and supplemental artifacts; if auditors require a BAA-signed chain, Priya has shared the draft.

I'll join the deep-dive and bring a short slide that maps artifacts to auditor questions. Priya — suggest we confirm whether PulseWell's auditors need originals or redacted samples.

—Neha
